purpose: Define MCP server connect/start/handshake/ready/error/stop lifecycle as tracked runtime state with bounded startup, request and cleanup behavior.

topics.name: MCP Transport and Lifecycle
topics.purpose: Define MCP server connect/start/handshake/ready/error/stop lifecycle as tracked runtime state with bounded startup, request and cleanup behavior.

semantics.start_rule: Configured server does not become ready until transport/handshake validation succeeds.
semantics.request_rule: Requests are bounded by timeout/concurrency/resource policy.
semantics.state_rule: Lifecycle state is runtime state, not server semantic identity.
semantics.restart_rule: Restart preserves configured semantic identity unless configuration explicitly changes it.
semantics.failure_rule: Unavailable server/tool is visible; runtime does not silently substitute another MCP server.

invariants.rule: MCP server identity, transport, tool schema, lifecycle and authority remain explicit and do not inherit trust from connectivity or advertised metadata.

hard_gates.condition: configured MCP server treated as ready before handshake
server failure silently falls back to unrelated MCP server
runtime state written as canonical server identity

references.purpose: MCP transport resources clean up on terminal paths.
MCP startup and requests are bounded.
